subject: desert tortoise
title: A Desert Tortoise Can Go a Year Without Drinking. Its Bladder Is the Trick

scenes.text: This tortoise can go over a year without a drink. The water is stored somewhere strange.
Desert tortoises live where ground temperatures pass forty degrees Celsius and rain is rare.
When it does rain, a tortoise drinks heavily from puddles.
Then it stores water in its bladder, up to about forty percent of its body weight, and reabsorbs it as needed.
It also spends about ninety-five percent of its life underground, in burrows that stay cool.
That's why rangers say never pick one up. A scared tortoise can empty its bladder and lose its water supply.

description:
The desert tortoise stores water in its bladder, up to about 40% of its body weight, and reabsorbs it as needed, letting adults go more than a year without drinking.
It spends about 95% of its life in burrows; the National Park Service warns that a handled tortoise may void its bladder and lose its stored water.
Would you have guessed a bladder could be a canteen?
first_comment: Desert tortoises can live 50 to 80 years. What desert animal should we cover next?
